headline: Adopted resolutions accepting a $5.5 million federal lead hazard grant, $1.65 million MassWorks grant, and $900,000 state preparedness grant.
summary: The council adopted grants, donations, ordinances, and a contract authorization, and confirmed two appointments. It denied an order on signs about civil immigration enforcement and a motion to postpone the meeting. Many resident petitions on sidewalks, streets, and traffic were referred to committees or placed on file.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 30, 2026 meeting, 8-0.
Granted Charter Communications permission for a conduit at 38-40 Southbridge St., 9-0.
Granted National Grid permission for a conduit at Florence St., 9-0. Similar grants were made for Grafton St., Grove St., and a jointly owned pole on West Boylston St.
Set public hearings for September 8, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. on National Grid conduit and pole requests at Velander St., Washington Sq., and Christine St.
Referred requests to replace picnic tables and repair the tennis/pickleball court at Morgan Landing to the Department of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery, 9-0.
Referred the request to ban the sale of miniature alcohol bottles to the Public Health and Human Services Committee, 9-0.
Referred sidewalk, street, lighting, and sewer petitions (items 8d through 8z, except 8r) to the Public Works Committee, 9-0.
Referred the request to convert Marmion Ave. from a private street to a public street to the Planning Board, 9-0.
Referred speed hump, stop sign, parking, and traffic petitions (items 9a through 9z, except 9h) to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 9-0.
Referred traffic study, speed hump, stop sign, and parking petitions (items 10a through 10r) to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 9-0.
Referred requests on spray park hours and Morgan Landing court lights to the Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation Committee, 9-0.
Referred the request to add Pickleball Court to the city website's park feature search to the City Manager, 9-0.
Referred three transportation communications, including the functional classification of streets and the Vision Zero Annual Report, to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 9-0.
Adopted an order allowing the purchasing director to procure a contract with a four-year term, 9-0.
Referred the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing agreement for 16-32 Lakeside Avenue and 18-20 Garland Avenue to the Economic Development Committee, 9-0.

Adopted as a group items 11.35A through 11.35V, 11.36A, and 11.37A through 11.37H, 9-0. These include a $900,000 state grant, a $5.5 million federal lead hazard grant, a $1.65 million MassWorks grant, and several donations.
Adopted requests on transit priority, a culvert report, traffic signs, and school bus speeding, 9-0.
Adopted an order asking for a review of Japanese knotweed overgrowth near 45 Marcy St., 9-0.
Referred the order on speed camera hearings (Rosen) to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 8-0 with King abstaining.
Adopted as amended an order asking for a report on public safety and cleanliness on the Worcester Common, 7-3.
Placed on file a request for a report on a July 24, 2026 sanitary sewer overflow near 23 Southwest Cutoff, 9-0.
Held under privilege a request for a public discussion on the closure of the Department of Justice investigation of the Worcester Police Department.
Adopted as amended an order asking the City Manager to meet with CSX about railcar idling and odors near Canterbury St., including information on the August 14, 2026 derailment, 9-0.
Adopted a request for a report on Department of Public Works staffing levels and open positions, 10-0.
Adopted a request to authorize a three-year software license agreement with Renaissance Learning for the Worcester Public Schools, 9-0.
Referred the zoning map amendment petition for 600 and 604 Lincoln St. to the Economic Development Committee, 9-0.
Accepted the committee report on the WRTA winter weather plan and placed it on file, 9-0.
Accepted and adopted sidewalk and street resurfacing orders for items 18a through 18j, 9-0.
Accepted committee reports on items 18k through 18s, including petitions placed on file and requests granted leave to withdraw, 9-0.
Voted to advertise proposed ordinances for traffic and parking items 19a through 19v, 9-0.
Accepted and adopted traffic orders for items 19w through 19z, including a crosswalk at Southbridge St. at Washburn St., 9-0.
Accepted and adopted traffic orders for items 20a through 20h, including truck restrictions on Ararat St. and Mount Ave., 9-0.
Accepted committee reports on traffic items 20i through 20z, which placed those petitions on file, 9-0.
Accepted committee reports on traffic items 21a through 21g, which placed those items on file, 9-0.
Ordained items 22a through 22n, including permit parking on Lodi Street and two-way travel on a portion of Beaver Street, 9-0.
Referred the annual survey and staffing process communications on the City Council Office to the Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 10-0.
Denied a motion to recommit the Worcester Redevelopment Authority appointment of Candice Mero-Carlson to the City Manager, 3-7.
Confirmed the appointment of Candice Mero-Carlson to the Worcester Redevelopment Authority, 7-3.
Confirmed the appointments of Jared Madison to the Trust Funds Commission and Che Anderson to the Civic Center Commission, 10-0.
Held under privilege a second time a municipal civilian review board report, 8-0.
Adopted an order asking for quarterly reports on outreach and police activity with unhoused individuals in the Canal District, 10-0.
Denied an order to install signage stating property may not be used for civil immigration enforcement, as amended, 5-5.
Denied an order requiring signage on civil immigration enforcement be listed in all appropriate languages, 5-5.
Referred the City Clerk's communication on one support staff vacancy in the City Council Office to the Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 10-0.
Took no action on six tabled items, including a rent control legal opinion request and a COVID-19 vaccination equity resolution.
Adopted the July 21, 2026 order asking for a report on efforts to enhance pedestrian safety near 137 Hope Ave., including lighting.
Adopted the July 21, 2026 order asking for a detailed report on the proposed zone change at 321 Greenwood St.
Denied a motion to postpone the August 18, 2026 meeting and move most items to September 8, 2026, 5-4.
Denied a motion to reconsider the postponement motion, 5-5.
